paper_title: Random Projection in the Brain and Computation with Assemblies of Neurons
classifications: Theory of computation → Models of computation
Theory of computation → Randomness, geometry and discrete structures
statement: 8. Learning. Can assemblies perform learning (supervised or unsupervised)? Simulations suggest that assemblies can learn well-separated half-spaces quite naturally. Can this be proved formally? And what more ambitious forms of learning through assemblies are possible? 9. Assemblies vs 1-step Projections. Are assemblies (created as the limit of iterated randomproject-and-cap) better for learning than 1-step (insect-like) projections? Is the recurrence of the mammalian brain a bonus or a handicap for learning? 10. Articulate a brain architecture for syntax (the building of syntactic trees) based on the assemblies operations project and merge and involving the medial temporal lobe, the superior temporal gyrus, and Broca’s area of the left human brain.
